content: With all the Fable 5 chatter, I'm curious whether anyone has pointed it a math paper and just said "formalize this!". Would be interested in hearing results? (in tokens and formalization results.)
If you do this, please make sure to include a #formalization.yaml !

I don't think I have the tokens to spare, but thanks for the pointer to formalization.yaml. I will add these to the formalizations I posted for Trellis and make generation of them automatic going forward.
So far , at least in my experience , Fable has been a colossal disappointment

Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 said:

So far , at least in my experience , Fable has been a colossal disappointment

What is the failure mode like?

My small anecdata is that I had been having Opus 4.8 attempting to make performance improvements to rpylean (sufficient for getting init finally type checking) for around 24 hours of token-time with no success.

Fable found the 3 issues I had missed in a half hour.

Wes Pegden said:

Yan Yablonovskiy 🇺🇦 said:

So far , at least in my experience , Fable has been a colossal disappointment

What is the failure mode like?

Well it depends on the use case , but in my case it would hallucinate or get wrong things about math Opus would not.

It tried to convince me 23/6 isn’t 3.83 ( to two decimal places ) for some reason which I wouldn’t expect this late in the game/ or from Opus. Then it conceded it was wrong etc but it did that like 10 times in a day and Opus didn’t do that nearly as much .

My experiences with Fable have been pretty good so far. It took a project that had been pretty thoroughly worked over with Opus and immediately found many improvements. It also found some significant performance improvements in an algorithmic project where Opus had called it quits.

Fable is SOTA on ProofBench:

https://www.vals.ai/benchmarks/proof_bench
Typically I have Codex review Opus' output before merging code, and it will find many—often important—issues. With Fable, Codex is finding far less potential bugs.

I used Fable to analyze Lean files of proof attempts of (non)halting of a specific Turing Machine that were produced by Opus. It did not find a better proof strategy but discovered some previously unknown facts (with proof) that apparently put this TM in a new category.
I have the impression that Fable is like Opus 4.8 with max thinking but 10x as fast.
RL for long horizon tasks is not a path towards better quality lean proofs.
If it delivers the result of what was previously a long-horizon task in minutes, is it still a long-horizon task?

@Wes Pegden I've been working on a system vaguely similar to your Trellis for the Jacobian challenge, and one thing I've noticed since Fable landed is that its answers to questions like "why did we just waste so much time on this dumb path?" or just "how can we improve?" has gotten much better, to the point that it's starting to feel like the system is actually capable of self-improvement.
It would be great to just run repeated isolated experiments on the same target with different models, etc. I did a bit of this early on but I don't keep redoing it as new model versions roll out...

Better in the sense of forcing users to "geographically diversify" their LLM providers? (If so, I agree.) Or better in some other sense?

This is kind of concerning, what will happen to open weigth models once they achieve the same capabilities. Huggin face even if created by europeans is hosted in US.
This means those kind of bans will also apply to open weigth models until hosting become also independent of US.
I'm sure we could talk endlessly about what's happening with Fable but it's off-topic for this Zulip.

(hopefully on topic) Does anyone have a very large scale OSS autoformalization project in flight (or quickly spin one up) and interested in pooling our collective 7 days of fable access for collaboration? I imagine a lot of folks will use it for new math results, but I would love to use some of my limitted access to advance formalization somehow.
